What · the second question

PDS Competence Model

The data-science capabilities that matter in pharma: 7 domains, 30 sub-areas and 123 competencies, each described at five levels. Use it to assess where people are today and to set targets.

7 domains · 30 sub-areas · 123 competenciesLast changed 2026-07-24

One scale for every competency

  1. L1Awarenessrecognises the concept; cannot yet do it.
  2. L2Familiaritycan do it from a template, with someone to ask.
  3. L3Proficiencyindependently delivers usable work on standard pharma problems.
  4. L4Masteryhandles non-standard cases; the person others escalate to.
  5. L5Expertisesets the standard; teaches, publishes, or open-sources.

Read the full level rubric and compare levels. L3 is the target working level, but nobody is expected to reach L3 in every competency.

    • Functional Thinking

Domain 3 Ethics, Legislation & Privacy

  • 3.1

    Data Science Ethics

    4 competencies

    • Concepts in data science ethics

  • 3.2

    Legislation

    2 competencies

    • Central legal and regulatory frameworks
    • Copyright and intellectual property concerns
  • 3.3

    Privacy

    6 competencies

    • Knowledge and compliance with privacy and data security regulations
    • Design and implementation of respectful and legal informed consent processes
    • Act with integrity when handling sensitive data
    • Application of legal and ethical standards to ensure responsible and competent data handling
    • Ensure that AI systems used are transparent and aligned with legal and ethical norms
    • Continuously update knowledge of ethical, legal, and technological developments in PDS
